goats.name: Chip
goats.bio: The fainting phenomenon! Chip is our distinguished Nigerian Dwarf buck with a special quirk—he has Myotonic genetics, meaning he faints when excited.
goats.backgroundStory: Chip is the patriarch of the Nigerian Dwarf herd. Standing taller than the others with a heavy bone structure, he commands respect—until he gets too excited and tips over! His 'fainting' is a harmless genetic trait that makes him all the more endearing. He's a gentle giant among dwarfs and loves a good scratch behind the ears.
goats.favoriteActivity: Overseeing his herd (from a horizontal position occasionally)

goats.name: Nugget
goats.bio: One of the 'Sweet Tooth' brothers. Nugget is a tri-colored buck kid with a refined dairy character.
goats.backgroundStory: Nugget is Brownie's brother and partner in crime. Smaller and more refined than Chip, he represents the classic dairy style of the Nigerian Dwarf breed. He's full of energy and is constantly challenging his brother to playful sparring matches.

goats.name: Brownie
goats.bio: Nugget's brother and partner in crime. Brownie sports a similar tri-color coat and loves to explore.
goats.backgroundStory: Brownie is the adventurous half of the kid duo. With his rich tri-color markings, he's a handsome young buck who is always the first to investigate a new toy or treat. He and Nugget are inseparable and bring a youthful energy to the buck pen.

goats.name: Snickerella
goats.bio: A sweet doe with a chocolate-caramel coat. Snickerella is as sweet as her name suggests.
goats.backgroundStory: Snickerella is a favorite for her beautiful Chamoisee coat that looks just like a chocolate bar. She has a lovely dairy conformation and a calm, motherly demeanor. She's often found grazing peacefully or waiting patiently for a treat.

goats.name: Oreana
goats.bio: Our 'Oreo' goat! Oreana features striking black and white markings and a high-contrast personality to match.
goats.backgroundStory: You can't miss Oreana in the pasture—her black and white markings stand out instantly. She's a doe with 'capacity' (room for babies!) and a friendly, outgoing nature. She loves attention and is often the first doe to greet visitors at the fence.

goats.name: Caramella
goats.bio: Golden and glowing, Caramella has a beautiful apricot coat and a gentle, sunny disposition.
goats.backgroundStory: Caramella brings a splash of gold to the herd. Her light, soft coat matches her gentle personality. She is a quiet, steady doe who gets along with everyone. Her sweet nature makes her a perfect ambassador for the breed.

goats.name: Cookie
goats.bio: Spotted and speckled like a cookies-and-cream treat. Cookie is a favorite for her unique roan coat.
goats.backgroundStory: Cookie is the artist of the group, sporting a multi-colored, speckled 'roan' coat that makes her truly unique. She's a curious doe who loves to see what's going on. Her distinctive look makes her easy to spot and hard to forget.

goats.name: Simba
goats.bio: The King of the Boer herd. Simba is a traditional Boer buck with a massive build and a gentle heart.
goats.backgroundStory: Simba lives up to his name. With his traditional red head and massive white body, he looks every bit the lion king of the farm. Despite his imposing size and thick muscular neck, he is a gentle giant who takes good care of his does. He is the sire of our future meat herd.

goats.name: Nala
goats.bio: The Queen of the herd. Nala (formerly Sarabi) is a traditional Boer doe with elegance and grace.
goats.backgroundStory: Nala is the queen to Simba's king. A traditional Boer doe with a feminine head and excellent width, she represents the ideal mother goat. She is calm, regal, and leads the doe herd with quiet confidence.

goats.name: Sarabi
goats.bio: Nala's close relative and loyal companion. Sarabi shares the traditional Boer markings and a calm nature.
goats.backgroundStory: Sarabi is Nala's right-hand doe. Related by blood and bond, they are often found together. She shares the classic Boer markings and the sturdy, productive build of the breed. She is a reliable and protective mother.

goats.name: Dippa
goats.bio: Named for her distinct markings. Dippa is a solid Boer doe who loves mealtime.
goats.backgroundStory: Dippa gets her name from her unique color pattern that looks like she was 'dipped' in paint. She's a robust Boer doe with a healthy appetite and a solid conformation. She's always the first to the feeder when the grain bucket rattles!

goats.name: Mary
goats.bio: Reliable and steady. Mary is a classic Boer doe with excellent conformation.
goats.backgroundStory: Mary is the rock of the Boer herd. She isn't the flashiest, but she is consistent, solid, and dependable. She has excellent structure for a meat goat and is a calm, no-nonsense mother who takes great care of her kids.

goats.name: Skora
goats.bio: Related to Nutella, Skora is a wonderful mother with a strong maternal instinct.
goats.backgroundStory: Skora is part of our 'sweet' family line in the Boer herd, related to Nutella. She combines the best of Boer genetics with a strong maternal instinct. She is attentive and caring, ensuring her kids—and sometimes others'—are safe and fed.

goats.name: Nutella
goats.bio: A sweet Boer doe with rich red-brown coloration. Nutella is as delightful as the spread she's named after.
goats.backgroundStory: Nutella stands out with her rich, reddish-brown coloration that gave her her name. Related to Skora, she brings a bit of color variety to the Boer herd. She's a sweet-natured doe who loves a treat and a head scratch.

goats.name: Nueggeta
goats.bio: Compact and cute. Nueggeta rounds out our Boer herd with her solid build and friendly face.
goats.backgroundStory: Don't let the name fool you—Nueggeta is a solid Boer doe! She has a compact, meaty build that is perfect for the breed standard. She's a friendly doe who fits right in with the herd, rounding out our group of seven lovely ladies.
